findings.source_passage: Blind and dumb might well be envied now.
findings.source_locator: Ahab to himself, after 'The greyheaded woodpecker tapping the hollow tree!'
findings.why_it_matters: This line is rhetorically striking and interpretively weighty — Ahab envying blindness and deafness to escape the symbol before him is a key articulation of his tormented consciousness; it precedes his observation about the line-tubs.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Blind and dumb might well be envied now.' in Ahab's soliloquy between the woodpecker image and 'See! that thing rests on two line-tubs.'

findings.source_passage: Art not thou the leg-maker? Look, did not this stump come from thy shop?
findings.source_locator: Ahab's second speech to the Carpenter, after 'Thy coffin lies handy to the vault.'
findings.why_it_matters: The draft collapses Ahab's two sequential challenges ('leg-maker?' and 'undertaker?') into a single line, erasing the leg/stump self-reference that makes the exchange personally grotesque and thematically charged — Ahab's own body parts are implicated.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full two-beat exchange: 'Art not thou the leg-maker? Look, did not this stump come from thy shop?' with the Carpenter's reply, then the 'undertaker?' question separately.

findings.source_passage: the reason why the grave-digger made music must have been because there was none in his spade, sir. But the caulking mallet is full of it.
findings.source_locator: Carpenter's reply to the singing question
findings.why_it_matters: The draft drops the Carpenter's 'Oh, I'm indifferent enough, sir, for that; but' preamble, losing the characteristic voice register of the Carpenter — his bumbling, hedging manner is a voice signature of this scene and shapes the comic texture of the exchange.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Carpenter's full reply including 'Oh, I'm indifferent enough, sir, for that; but' before the spade/mallet contrast.

findings.source_passage: Um, um; go on. / I was about to say, sir, that——
findings.source_locator: After 'Why, faith, sir, it's only a sort of exclamation-like—that's all, sir.'
findings.why_it_matters: The draft omits Ahab's 'Um, um; go on.' beat, which is a small but characteristic moment of Ahab's weary irony before he abruptly cuts the Carpenter off — the comedic rhythm of the interruption depends on this setup.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Um, um; go on.' before the Carpenter's 'I was about to say, sir, that——' to preserve the comic timing of Ahab's interruption.

summary: No high-severity signature losses; three medium findings involve flattening of the leg/stump exchange, the Carpenter's hedging voice, and the dropped 'Blind and dumb' line, but the chapter's major interpretive set-pieces — the jack-of-all-trades speech, the immortality-preserver soliloquy, and the Equator speech — are preserved with sufficient fidelity.
